# ==================== ShuffleNet v1 ====================
class ShuffleBlock(nn.Module):
    """
    Channel Shuffle operation: Enables information flow across channel groups
    Key innovation of ShuffleNet for efficient group convolutions
    """
    def __init__(self, groups):
        super(ShuffleBlock, self).__init__()
        self.groups = groups
    
    def forward(self, x):
        batch_size, num_channels, height, width = x.size()
        channels_per_group = num_channels // self.groups
        
        # Reshape and transpose for shuffling
        x = x.view(batch_size, self.groups, channels_per_group, height, width)
        x = x.transpose(1, 2).contiguous()
        x = x.view(batch_size, -1, height, width)
        
        return x


class ShuffleNetUnitV1(nn.Module):
    """
    ShuffleNet v1 Unit: Combines group convolution with channel shuffle
    """
    def __init__(self, in_channels, out_channels, groups, stride=1):
        super(ShuffleNetUnitV1, self).__init__()
        self.stride = stride
        mid_channels = out_channels // 4
        
        if stride == 2:
            out_channels = out_channels - in_channels
        
        # First pointwise group convolution
        self.compress = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(in_channels, mid_channels, 1, groups=groups, bias=False),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(mid_channels),
            nn.ReLU(inplace=True)
        )
        
        self.shuffle = ShuffleBlock(groups)
        
        # Depthwise convolution
        self.depthwise = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(mid_channels, mid_channels, 3, stride, 1, 
                     groups=mid_channels, bias=False),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(mid_channels)
        )
        
        # Second pointwise group convolution
        self.expand = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(mid_channels, out_channels, 1, groups=groups, bias=False),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(out_channels)
        )
        
        # Shortcut
        if stride == 2:
            self.shortcut = nn.AvgPool2d(3, stride=2, padding=1)
        
        self.relu = nn.ReLU(inplace=True)
    
    def forward(self, x):
        out = self.compress(x)
        out = self.shuffle(out)
        out = self.depthwise(out)
        out = self.expand(out)
        
        if self.stride == 1:
            out = out + x
        else:
            out = torch.cat([out, self.shortcut(x)], 1)
        
        return self.relu(out)


class ShuffleNetV1(nn.Module):
    """
    ShuffleNet v1: Extremely efficient CNN using pointwise group convolutions
    and channel shuffle operations
    """
    def __init__(self, num_classes=1000, groups=3, width_mult=1.0):
        super(ShuffleNetV1, self).__init__()
        self.groups = groups
        
        # Output channels for different group configurations
        if groups == 1:
            out_channels = [24, 144, 288, 576]
        elif groups == 2:
            out_channels = [24, 200, 400, 800]
        elif groups == 3:
            out_channels = [24, 240, 480, 960]
        elif groups == 4:
            out_channels = [24, 272, 544, 1088]
        elif groups == 8:
            out_channels = [24, 384, 768, 1536]
        else:
            raise ValueError("Groups must be 1, 2, 3, 4, or 8")
        
        out_channels = [int(c * width_mult) for c in out_channels]
        
        # First convolution layer
        self.conv1 = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(3, out_channels[0], 3, 2, 1, bias=False),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(out_channels[0]),
            nn.ReLU(inplace=True)
        )
        
        self.maxpool = nn.MaxPool2d(3, 2, 1)
        
        # Stage 2
        self.stage2 = self._make_stage(out_channels[0], out_channels[1], 4)
        # Stage 3
        self.stage3 = self._make_stage(out_channels[1], out_channels[2], 8)
        # Stage 4
        self.stage4 = self._make_stage(out_channels[2], out_channels[3], 4)
        
        self.avgpool = nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1)
        self.fc = nn.Linear(out_channels[3], num_classes)
    
    def _make_stage(self, in_channels, out_channels, num_blocks):
        layers = []
        # First block with stride 2
        layers.append(ShuffleNetUnitV1(in_channels, out_channels, 
                                       self.groups, stride=2))
        # Remaining blocks with stride 1
        for _ in range(num_blocks - 1):
            layers.append(ShuffleNetUnitV1(out_channels, out_channels, 
                                          self.groups, stride=1))
        return nn.Sequential(*layers)
    
    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.conv1(x)
        x = self.maxpool(x)
        x = self.stage2(x)
        x = self.stage3(x)
        x = self.stage4(x)
        x = self.avgpool(x)
        x = x.view(x.size(0), -1)
        x = self.fc(x)
        return x


# ==================== ShuffleNet v2 ====================
class ShuffleNetUnitV2(nn.Module):
    """
    ShuffleNet v2 Unit: Improved design with channel split operation
    More efficient than v1 with better accuracy
    """
    def __init__(self, in_channels, out_channels, stride):
        super(ShuffleNetUnitV2, self).__init__()
        self.stride = stride
        branch_features = out_channels // 2
        
        if stride == 1:
            assert in_channels == branch_features * 2
        
        if stride > 1:
            # When stride > 1, process all channels
            self.branch1 = nn.Sequential(
                # Depthwise conv
                nn.Conv2d(in_channels, in_channels, 3, stride, 1, 
                         groups=in_channels, bias=False),
                nn.BatchNorm2d(in_channels),
                # Pointwise conv
                nn.Conv2d(in_channels, branch_features, 1, bias=False),
                nn.BatchNorm2d(branch_features),
                nn.ReLU(inplace=True)
            )
        else:
            self.branch1 = nn.Sequential()
        
        self.branch2 = nn.Sequential(
            # Pointwise conv
            nn.Conv2d(in_channels if stride > 1 else branch_features,
                     branch_features, 1, bias=False),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(branch_features),
            nn.ReLU(inplace=True),
            # Depthwise conv
            nn.Conv2d(branch_features, branch_features, 3, stride, 1,
                     groups=branch_features, bias=False),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(branch_features),
            # Pointwise conv
            nn.Conv2d(branch_features, branch_features, 1, bias=False),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(branch_features),
            nn.ReLU(inplace=True)
        )
    
    def forward(self, x):
        if self.stride == 1:
            # Channel split
            x1, x2 = x.chunk(2, dim=1)
            out = torch.cat([x1, self.branch2(x2)], dim=1)
        else:
            out = torch.cat([self.branch1(x), self.branch2(x)], dim=1)
        
        # Channel shuffle
        batch_size, num_channels, height, width = out.size()
        out = out.view(batch_size, 2, num_channels // 2, height, width)
        out = out.transpose(1, 2).contiguous()
        out = out.view(batch_size, -1, height, width)
        
        return out


class ShuffleNetV2(nn.Module):
    """
    ShuffleNet v2: Optimized for actual inference speed
    Uses channel split and efficient block design
    """
    def __init__(self, num_classes=1000, model_size='1.0x'):
        super(ShuffleNetV2, self).__init__()
        
        # Configuration for different model sizes
        if model_size == '0.5x':
            channels = [24, 48, 96, 192, 1024]
        elif model_size == '1.0x':
            channels = [24, 116, 232, 464, 1024]
        elif model_size == '1.5x':
            channels = [24, 176, 352, 704, 1024]
        elif model_size == '2.0x':
            channels = [24, 244, 488, 976, 2048]
        else:
            raise ValueError("Model size must be 0.5x, 1.0x, 1.5x, or 2.0x")
        
        # First convolution
        self.conv1 = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(3, channels[0], 3, 2, 1, bias=False),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(channels[0]),
            nn.ReLU(inplace=True)
        )
        
        self.maxpool = nn.MaxPool2d(3, 2, 1)
        
        # Build stages
        self.stage2 = self._make_stage(channels[0], channels[1], 4)
        self.stage3 = self._make_stage(channels[1], channels[2], 8)
        self.stage4 = self._make_stage(channels[2], channels[3], 4)
        
        self.conv5 = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(channels[3], channels[4], 1, bias=False),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(channels[4]),
            nn.ReLU(inplace=True)
        )
        
        self.avgpool = nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1)
        self.fc = nn.Linear(channels[4], num_classes)
    
    def _make_stage(self, in_channels, out_channels, num_blocks):
        layers = []
        # First block with stride 2
        layers.append(ShuffleNetUnitV2(in_channels, out_channels, stride=2))
        # Remaining blocks with stride 1
        for _ in range(num_blocks - 1):
            layers.append(ShuffleNetUnitV2(out_channels, out_channels, stride=1))
        return nn.Sequential(*layers)
    
    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.conv1(x)
        x = self.maxpool(x)
        x = self.stage2(x)
        x = self.stage3(x)
        x = self.stage4(x)
        x = self.conv5(x)
        x = self.avgpool(x)
        x = x.view(x.size(0), -1)
        x = self.fc(x)
        return x


# ==================== GhostNet ====================
class GhostModule(nn.Module):
    """
    Ghost Module: Generates more features from cheap operations
    Key innovation: generate "ghost" features from intrinsic features
    Reduces computation significantly
    """
    def __init__(self, in_channels, out_channels, kernel_size=1, 
                 ratio=2, dw_size=3, stride=1, relu=True):
        super(GhostModule, self).__init__()
        self.out_channels = out_channels
        init_channels = out_channels // ratio
        new_channels = out_channels - init_channels
        
        # Primary convolution (generates intrinsic features)
        self.primary_conv = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(in_channels, init_channels, kernel_size, stride, 
                     kernel_size // 2, bias=False),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(init_channels),
            nn.ReLU(inplace=True) if relu else nn.Sequential()
        )
        
        # Cheap operation (generates ghost features)
        self.cheap_operation = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(init_channels, new_channels, dw_size, 1, dw_size // 2,
                     groups=init_channels, bias=False),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(new_channels),
            nn.ReLU(inplace=True) if relu else nn.Sequential()
        )
    
    def forward(self, x):
        x1 = self.primary_conv(x)
        x2 = self.cheap_operation(x1)
        out = torch.cat([x1, x2], dim=1)
        return out[:, :self.out_channels, :, :]


class GhostBottleneck(nn.Module):
    """
    Ghost Bottleneck: Building block for GhostNet
    Uses Ghost modules instead of standard convolutions
    """
    def __init__(self, in_channels, mid_channels, out_channels, 
                 kernel_size, stride, use_se=False):
        super(GhostBottleneck, self).__init__()
        self.stride = stride
        
        # Pointwise expansion
        self.ghost1 = GhostModule(in_channels, mid_channels, relu=True)
        
        # Depthwise convolution
        if stride == 2:
            self.conv_dw = nn.Conv2d(mid_channels, mid_channels, kernel_size, 
                                    stride, kernel_size // 2, 
```python
                                    groups=mid_channels, bias=False)
            self.bn_dw = nn.BatchNorm2d(mid_channels)
        
        # Squeeze-and-Excitation
        if use_se:
            self.se = SqueezeExcitation(mid_channels, mid_channels // 4)
        else:
            self.se = None
        
        # Pointwise projection
        self.ghost2 = GhostModule(mid_channels, out_channels, relu=False)
        
        # Shortcut
        if stride == 1 and in_channels == out_channels:
            self.shortcut = nn.Sequential()
        else:
            self.shortcut = nn.Sequential(
                nn.Conv2d(in_channels, in_channels, kernel_size, stride,
                         kernel_size // 2, groups=in_channels, bias=False),
                nn.BatchNorm2d(in_channels),
                nn.Conv2d(in_channels, out_channels, 1, bias=False),
                nn.BatchNorm2d(out_channels)
            )
    
    def forward(self, x):
        residual = x
        
        # First ghost module
        x = self.ghost1(x)
        
        # Depthwise convolution
        if self.stride == 2:
            x = self.conv_dw(x)
            x = self.bn_dw(x)
        
        # Squeeze-and-Excitation
        if self.se is not None:
            x = self.se(x)
        
        # Second ghost module
        x = self.ghost2(x)
        
        return x + self.shortcut(residual)


class GhostNet(nn.Module):
    """
    GhostNet: Efficient neural network using Ghost modules
    Generates redundant features from cheap operations
    Achieves similar accuracy to MobileNetV3 with lower computational cost
    """
    def __init__(self, num_classes=1000, width_mult=1.0):
        super(GhostNet, self).__init__()
        
        # [kernel, exp, out, se, stride]
        config = [
            # Stage 1
            [3, 16, 16, False, 1],
            # Stage 2
            [3, 48, 24, False, 2],
            [3, 72, 24, False, 1],
            # Stage 3
            [5, 72, 40, True, 2],
            [5, 120, 40, True, 1],
            # Stage 4
            [3, 240, 80, False, 2],
            [3, 200, 80, False, 1],
            [3, 184, 80, False, 1],
            [3, 184, 80, False, 1],
            [3, 480, 112, True, 1],
            [3, 672, 112, True, 1],
            # Stage 5
            [5, 672, 160, True, 2],
            [5, 960, 160, False, 1],
            [5, 960, 160, True, 1],
            [5, 960, 160, False, 1],
            [5, 960, 160, True, 1],
        ]
        
        # First convolution
        output_channel = int(16 * width_mult)
        self.conv_stem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(3, output_channel, 3, 2, 1, bias=False),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(output_channel),
            nn.ReLU(inplace=True)
        )
        
        input_channel = output_channel
        
        # Build ghost bottlenecks
        stages = []
        for k, exp, c, se, s in config:
            output_channel = int(c * width_mult)
            hidden_channel = int(exp * width_mult)
            stages.append(GhostBottleneck(input_channel, hidden_channel,
                                         output_channel, k, s, se))
            input_channel = output_channel
        
        self.blocks = nn.Sequential(*stages)
        
        # Final layers
        output_channel = int(960 * width_mult)
        self.conv_head = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(input_channel, output_channel, 1, bias=False),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(output_channel),
            nn.ReLU(inplace=True)
        )
        
        self.avgpool = nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1)
        self.classifier = nn.Linear(output_channel, num_classes)
        
        self._initialize_weights()
    
    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.conv_stem(x)
        x = self.blocks(x)
        x = self.conv_head(x)
        x = self.avgpool(x)
        x = x.view(x.size(0), -1)
        x = self.classifier(x)
        return x
    
    def _initialize_weights(self):
        for m in self.modules():
            if isinstance(m, nn.Conv2d):
                nn.init.kaiming_normal_(m.weight, mode='fan_out', 
                                       nonlinearity='relu')
            elif isinstance(m, nn.BatchNorm2d):
                nn.init.ones_(m.weight)
                nn.init.zeros_(m.bias)


# ==================== ESPNet ====================
class BRUnit(nn.Module):
    """
    Batch Normalization + ReLU Unit
    """
    def __init__(self, num_features):
        super(BRUnit, self).__init__()
        self.bn = nn.BatchNorm2d(num_features)
        self.relu = nn.ReLU(inplace=True)
    
    def forward(self, x):
        return self.relu(self.bn(x))


class ESPModule(nn.Module):
    """
    Efficient Spatial Pyramid (ESP) Module
    Uses point-wise convolutions and spatial pyramid of dilated convolutions
    Achieves large effective receptive field efficiently
    """
    def __init__(self, in_channels, out_channels, num_branches=4, 
                 add_input=True):
        super(ESPModule, self).__init__()
        self.num_branches = num_branches
        self.add_input = add_input
        
        # Reduce channels
        n = out_channels // num_branches
        n1 = out_channels - (num_branches - 1) * n
        
        # Point-wise convolution to reduce dimensions
        self.reduce = nn.Conv2d(in_channels, n, 1, bias=False)
        
        # Dilated convolutions with different dilation rates
        self.branches = nn.ModuleList()
        for i in range(num_branches):
            dilation = 2 ** i
            if i == 0:
                self.branches.append(
                    nn.Conv2d(n, n1, 3, padding=dilation, 
                             dilation=dilation, bias=False)
                )
            else:
                self.branches.append(
                    nn.Conv2d(n, n, 3, padding=dilation, 
                             dilation=dilation, bias=False)
                )
        
        self.bn = BRUnit(out_channels)
        
        # Projection for residual connection if needed
        if add_input and in_channels != out_channels:
            self.project = nn.Sequential(
                nn.Conv2d(in_channels, out_channels, 1, bias=False),
                nn.BatchNorm2d(out_channels)
            )
        else:
            self.project = None
    
    def forward(self, x):
        # Reduce dimensions
        reduced = self.reduce(x)
        
        # Hierarchical feature fusion (HFF)
        outputs = []
        for i, branch in enumerate(self.branches):
            if i == 0:
                outputs.append(branch(reduced))
            else:
                # Add previous output to current branch input
                outputs.append(branch(reduced + outputs[i-1]))
        
        # Concatenate all branch outputs
        out = torch.cat(outputs, dim=1)
        out = self.bn(out)
        
        # Add input (residual connection)
        if self.add_input:
            if self.project is not None:
                out = out + self.project(x)
            else:
                out = out + x
        
        return out


class DownSampler(nn.Module):
    """
    Downsampling module for ESPNet
    Combines strided convolution with max pooling
    """
    def __init__(self, in_channels, out_channels):
        super(DownSampler, self).__init__()
        
        n = out_channels - in_channels
        
        self.conv = nn.Conv2d(in_channels, n, 3, stride=2, padding=1, bias=False)
        self.pool = nn.MaxPool2d(2, stride=2)
        self.bn = BRUnit(out_channels)
    
    def forward(self, x):
        conv_out = self.conv(x)
        pool_out = self.pool(x)
        
        out = torch.cat([conv_out, pool_out], dim=1)
        out = self.bn(out)
        
        return out


class ESPNet(nn.Module):
    """
    ESPNet: Efficient Spatial Pyramid Network
    Designed for semantic segmentation and edge devices
    Uses ESP modules for efficient multi-scale feature extraction
    """
    def __init__(self, num_classes=1000, scale=1.0):
        super(ESPNet, self).__init__()
        
        # Scale channels
        channels = [int(c * scale) for c in [16, 64, 128, 256]]
        
        # Level 1: Standard convolution
        self.level1 = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(3, channels[0], 3, 2, 1, bias=False),
            BRUnit(channels[0])
        )
        
        # Level 2: Downsampler + ESP modules
        self.level2_0 = DownSampler(channels[0], channels[1])
        self.level2 = nn.Sequential(
            ESPModule(channels[1], channels[1]),
            ESPModule(channels[1], channels[1]),
            ESPModule(channels[1], channels[1])
        )
        
        # Level 3: Downsampler + ESP modules
        self.level3_0 = DownSampler(channels[1], channels[2])
        self.level3 = nn.Sequential(
            ESPModule(channels[2], channels[2]),
            ESPModule(channels[2], channels[2]),
            ESPModule(channels[2], channels[2]),
            ESPModule(channels[2], channels[2]),
            ESPModule(channels[2], channels[2]),
            ESPModule(channels[2], channels[2]),
            ESPModule(channels[2], channels[2]),
            ESPModule(channels[2], channels[2])
        )
        
        # Level 4: For classification
        self.level4_0 = DownSampler(channels[2], channels[3])
        self.level4 = nn.Sequential(
            ESPModule(channels[3], channels[3]),
            ESPModule(channels[3], channels[3]),
            ESPModule(channels[3], channels[3])
        )
        
        # Classification head
        self.avgpool = nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1)
        self.classifier = nn.Linear(channels[3], num_classes)
        
        self._initialize_weights()
    
    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.level1(x)
        
        x = self.level2_0(x)
        x = self.level2(x)
        
        x = self.level3_0(x)
        x = self.level3(x)
        
        x = self.level4_0(x)
        x = self.level4(x)
        
        x = self.avgpool(x)
        x = x.view(x.size(0), -1)
        x = self.classifier(x)
        
        return x
    
    def _initialize_weights(self):
        for m in self.modules():
            if isinstance(m, nn.Conv2d):
                nn.init.kaiming_normal_(m.weight, mode='fan_out', 
                                       nonlinearity='relu')
                if m.bias is not None:
                    nn.init.zeros_(m.bias)
            elif isinstance(m, nn.BatchNorm2d):
                nn.init.ones_(m.weight)
                nn.init.zeros_(m.bias)
            elif isinstance(m, nn.Linear):
                nn.init.normal_(m.weight, 0, 0.01)
                nn.init.zeros_(m.bias)


# ==================== EfficientNet-Lite ====================
class MBConvBlock(nn.Module):
    """
    Mobile Inverted Bottleneck Convolution Block
    Used in EfficientNet-Lite (simplified version without SE)
    """
    def __init__(self, in_channels, out_channels, expand_ratio, 
                 kernel_size, stride, drop_connect_rate=0.2):
        super(MBConvBlock, self).__init__()
        self.stride = stride
        self.drop_connect_rate = drop_connect_rate
        self.use_residual = (stride == 1 and in_channels == out_channels)
        
        # Expansion phase
        hidden_dim = in_channels * expand_ratio
        self.expand = expand_ratio != 1
        
        if self.expand:
            self.expand_conv = nn.Sequential(
                nn.Conv2d(in_channels, hidden_dim, 1, bias=False),
                nn.BatchNorm2d(hidden_dim),
                nn.ReLU6(inplace=True)
            )
        
        # Depthwise convolution
        self.depthwise_conv = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(hidden_dim, hidden_dim, kernel_size, stride,
                     kernel_size // 2, groups=hidden_dim, bias=False),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(hidden_dim),
            nn.ReLU6(inplace=True)
        )
        
        # Output projection
        self.project_conv = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(hidden_dim, out_channels, 1, bias=False),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(out_channels)
        )
    
    def forward(self, x):
        identity = x
        
        # Expansion
        if self.expand:
            x = self.expand_conv(x)
        
        # Depthwise
        x = self.depthwise_conv(x)
        
        # Projection
        x = self.project_conv(x)
        
        # Skip connection with drop connect
        if self.use_residual:
            if self.training and self.drop_connect_rate > 0:
                # Stochastic depth
                keep_prob = 1 - self.drop_connect_rate
                random_tensor = keep_prob + torch.rand(
                    [x.shape[0], 1, 1, 1], dtype=x.dtype, device=x.device
                )
                binary_tensor = torch.floor(random_tensor)
                x = x / keep_prob * binary_tensor
            x = x + identity
        
        return x


class EfficientNetLite(nn.Module):
    """
    EfficientNet-Lite: Optimized for mobile/edge devices
    Removes squeeze-
```python
    """
    EfficientNet-Lite: Optimized for mobile/edge devices
    Removes squeeze-and-excitation blocks and uses ReLU6 instead of Swish
    Designed for integer-only quantization
    """
    def __init__(self, num_classes=1000, width_mult=1.0, depth_mult=1.0, 
                 dropout_rate=0.2):
        super(EfficientNetLite, self).__init__()
        
        # [expand_ratio, channels, num_blocks, stride, kernel_size]
        config = [
            [1, 16, 1, 1, 3],
            [6, 24, 2, 2, 3],
            [6, 40, 2, 2, 5],
            [6, 80, 3, 2, 3],
            [6, 112, 3, 1, 5],
            [6, 192, 4, 2, 5],
            [6, 320, 1, 1, 3],
        ]
        
        # Stem
        out_channels = self._round_filters(32, width_mult)
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(3, out_channels, 3, 2, 1, bias=False),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(out_channels),
            nn.ReLU6(inplace=True)
        )
        
        # Build blocks
        in_channels = out_channels
        blocks = []
        
        for expand_ratio, c, n, s, k in config:
            out_channels = self._round_filters(c, width_mult)
            num_blocks = self._round_repeats(n, depth_mult)
            
            for i in range(num_blocks):
                stride = s if i == 0 else 1
                blocks.append(MBConvBlock(
                    in_channels, out_channels, expand_ratio, k, stride
                ))
                in_channels = out_channels
        
        self.blocks = nn.Sequential(*blocks)
        
        # Head
        final_channels = self._round_filters(1280, width_mult)
        self.head = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(in_channels, final_channels, 1, bias=False),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(final_channels),
            nn.ReLU6(inplace=True)
        )
        
        self.avgpool = nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1)
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout_rate)
        self.classifier = nn.Linear(final_channels, num_classes)
        
        self._initialize_weights()
    
    def _round_filters(self, filters, width_mult):
        """Round number of filters based on width multiplier."""
        if width_mult == 1.0:
            return filters
        filters *= width_mult
        new_filters = int(filters + 4) // 8 * 8
        new_filters = max(8, new_filters)
        if new_filters < 0.9 * filters:
            new_filters += 8
        return int(new_filters)
    
    def _round_repeats(self, repeats, depth_mult):
        """Round number of repeats based on depth multiplier."""
        if depth_mult == 1.0:
            return repeats
        return int(repeats * depth_mult)
    
    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.stem(x)
        x = self.blocks(x)
        x = self.head(x)
        x = self.avgpool(x)
        x = x.view(x.size(0), -1)
        x = self.dropout(x)
        x = self.classifier(x)
        return x
    
    def _initialize_weights(self):
        for m in self.modules():
            if isinstance(m, nn.Conv2d):
                nn.init.kaiming_normal_(m.weight, mode='fan_out')
                if m.bias is not None:
                    nn.init.zeros_(m.bias)
            elif isinstance(m, nn.BatchNorm2d):
                nn.init.ones_(m.weight)
                nn.init.zeros_(m.bias)
            elif isinstance(m, nn.Linear):
                nn.init.normal_(m.weight, 0, 0.01)
                nn.init.zeros_(m.bias)


# ==================== MicroNet ====================
class DynamicShiftMax(nn.Module):
    """
    Dynamic Shift-Max operation for MicroNet
    Efficient alternative to depthwise convolutions
    """
    def __init__(self, channels, kernel_size=3, stride=1, reduction=4):
        super(DynamicShiftMax, self).__init__()
        self.kernel_size = kernel_size
        self.stride = stride
        self.channels = channels
        
        # Generate shift patterns
        self.shift_channels = channels // 4
        
        # Point-wise convolution for attention
        self.pw_conv = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(channels, channels // reduction, 1, bias=False),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(channels // reduction),
            nn.ReLU(inplace=True),
            nn.Conv2d(channels // reduction, kernel_size * kernel_size, 1, bias=False)
        )
        
    def forward(self, x):
        batch_size, channels, height, width = x.size()
        
        # Apply spatial shifts
        shifted_features = []
        
        # Center (no shift)
        shifted_features.append(x[:, :self.shift_channels])
        
        # Up shift
        shifted_features.append(
            F.pad(x[:, self.shift_channels:2*self.shift_channels, 1:, :], 
                  (0, 0, 0, 1))
        )
        
        # Down shift
        shifted_features.append(
            F.pad(x[:, 2*self.shift_channels:3*self.shift_channels, :-1, :], 
                  (0, 0, 1, 0))
        )
        
        # Left shift
        shifted_features.append(
            F.pad(x[:, 3*self.shift_channels:, :, 1:], 
                  (0, 1, 0, 0))
        )
        
        # Concatenate shifted features
        out = torch.cat(shifted_features, dim=1)
        
        # Apply stride if needed
        if self.stride > 1:
            out = F.avg_pool2d(out, self.stride)
        
        return out


class MicroBlock(nn.Module):
    """
    MicroBlock: Extremely efficient building block for MicroNet
    Uses dynamic shift-max and lite residual connections
    """
    def __init__(self, in_channels, out_channels, kernel_size=3, 
                 stride=1, expand_ratio=6):
        super(MicroBlock, self).__init__()
        self.stride = stride
        self.use_residual = (stride == 1 and in_channels == out_channels)
        
        hidden_dim = in_channels * expand_ratio
        
        # Expansion
        self.expand = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(in_channels, hidden_dim, 1, bias=False),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(hidden_dim),
            nn.ReLU6(inplace=True)
        ) if expand_ratio != 1 else nn.Identity()
        
        # Dynamic shift-max or depthwise conv
        self.spatial = DynamicShiftMax(hidden_dim, kernel_size, stride)
        
        # Projection
        self.project = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(hidden_dim, out_channels, 1, bias=False),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(out_channels)
        )
    
    def forward(self, x):
        identity = x
        
        out = self.expand(x)
        out = self.spatial(out)
        out = self.project(out)
        
        if self.use_residual:
            out = out + identity
        
        return out


class MicroNet(nn.Module):
    """
    MicroNet: Ultra-lightweight network for resource-constrained devices
    Winner of NeurIPS 2019 MicroNet Challenge
    Optimizes for both FLOPs and parameter count
    """
    def __init__(self, num_classes=1000, width_mult=1.0):
        super(MicroNet, self).__init__()
        
        # [expand_ratio, out_channels, num_blocks, stride]
        config = [
            [1, 8, 1, 1],
            [6, 12, 2, 2],
            [6, 16, 2, 2],
            [6, 32, 3, 2],
            [6, 64, 3, 2],
            [6, 96, 2, 1],
        ]
        
        # Stem
        input_channel = self._make_divisible(12 * width_mult)
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(3, input_channel, 3, 2, 1, bias=False),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(input_channel),
            nn.ReLU6(inplace=True)
        )
        
        # Build blocks
        layers = []
        for t, c, n, s in config:
            output_channel = self._make_divisible(c * width_mult)
            for i in range(n):
                stride = s if i == 0 else 1
                layers.append(MicroBlock(input_channel, output_channel, 
                                        stride=stride, expand_ratio=t))
                input_channel = output_channel
        
        self.layers = nn.Sequential(*layers)
        
        # Head
        self.conv_head = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(input_channel, 1024, 1, bias=False),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(1024),
            nn.ReLU6(inplace=True)
        )
        
        self.avgpool = nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1)
        self.classifier = nn.Linear(1024, num_classes)
        
        self._initialize_weights()
    
    def _make_divisible(self, v, divisor=8):
        """Ensure channel number is divisible by divisor."""
        new_v = max(divisor, int(v + divisor / 2) // divisor * divisor)
        if new_v < 0.9 * v:
            new_v += divisor
        return new_v
    
    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.stem(x)
        x = self.layers(x)
        x = self.conv_head(x)
        x = self.avgpool(x)
        x = x.view(x.size(0), -1)
        x = self.classifier(x)
        return x
    
    def _initialize_weights(self):
        for m in self.modules():
            if isinstance(m, nn.Conv2d):
                nn.init.kaiming_normal_(m.weight, mode='fan_out')
                if m.bias is not None:
                    nn.init.zeros_(m.bias)
            elif isinstance(m, nn.BatchNorm2d):
                nn.init.ones_(m.weight)
                nn.init.zeros_(m.bias)
            elif isinstance(m, nn.Linear):
                nn.init.normal_(m.weight, 0, 0.01)
                nn.init.zeros_(m.bias)


# ==================== MCUNet ====================
class TinyNAS_Block(nn.Module):
    """
    TinyNAS Block: Searched block for MCUNet
    Optimized for microcontroller deployment
    """
    def __init__(self, in_channels, out_channels, kernel_size, 
                 stride, expand_ratio):
        super(TinyNAS_Block, self).__init__()
        self.stride = stride
        self.use_residual = (stride == 1 and in_channels == out_channels)
        
        hidden_dim = round(in_channels * expand_ratio)
        
        layers = []
        
        # Expansion
        if expand_ratio != 1:
            layers.extend([
                nn.Conv2d(in_channels, hidden_dim, 1, bias=False),
                nn.BatchNorm2d(hidden_dim),
                nn.ReLU6(inplace=True)
            ])
        
        # Depthwise
        layers.extend([
            nn.Conv2d(hidden_dim, hidden_dim, kernel_size, stride,
                     kernel_size // 2, groups=hidden_dim, bias=False),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(hidden_dim),
            nn.ReLU6(inplace=True)
        ])
        
        # Projection
        layers.extend([
            nn.Conv2d(hidden_dim, out_channels, 1, bias=False),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(out_channels)
        ])
        
        self.conv = nn.Sequential(*layers)
    
    def forward(self, x):
        if self.use_residual:
            return x + self.conv(x)
        return self.conv(x)


class MCUNet(nn.Module):
    """
    MCUNet: Tiny Deep Learning on IoT Devices
    Co-designed with TinyEngine for efficient inference on microcontrollers
    Achieves ImageNet-scale inference on microcontrollers with <1MB memory
    """
    def __init__(self, num_classes=1000, net_config='mcunet-in3'):

        if net_config == 'mcunet-in3':  # 320KB SRAM

                [4, 16, 2, 2, 3],
                [4, 24, 2, 2, 5],
                [4, 32, 2, 2, 3],
                [6, 64, 2, 2, 5],
                [6, 96, 1, 1, 3],
            ]
            first_conv_out = 8
            last_conv_out = 320
        elif net_config == 'mcunet-in2':  # 256KB SRAM
            config = [
                [1, 6, 1, 1, 3],
                [4, 12, 2, 2, 3],
                [4, 20, 2, 2, 5],
                [4, 28, 2, 2, 3],
                [6, 56, 2, 2, 5],
                [6, 88, 1, 1, 3],
            ]
            first_conv_out = 6
            last_conv_out = 280
        else:  # mcunet-in1, 192KB SRAM
            config = [
                [1, 6, 1, 1, 3],
                [4, 10, 2, 2, 3],
                [4, 16, 2, 2, 5],
                [4, 24, 2, 2, 3],
                [6, 48, 2, 2, 5],
                [6, 72, 1, 1, 3],
            ]
            first_conv_out = 6
            last_conv_out = 240
        
        # First convolution
        self.first_conv = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv
```python
            nn.Conv2d(3, first_conv_out, 3, 2, 1, bias=False),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(first_conv_out),
            nn.ReLU6(inplace=True)
        )
        
        # Build blocks
        layers = []
        in_channels = first_conv_out
        
        for t, c, n, s, k in config:
            out_channels = c
            for i in range(n):
                stride = s if i == 0 else 1
                layers.append(TinyNAS_Block(in_channels, out_channels, 
                                           k, stride, t))
                in_channels = out_channels
        
        self.blocks = nn.Sequential(*layers)
        
        # Last convolution
        self.last_conv = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(in_channels, last_conv_out, 1, bias=False),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(last_conv_out),
            nn.ReLU6(inplace=True)
        )
        
        # Classifier
        self.avgpool = nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1)
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(0.2)
        self.classifier = nn.Linear(last_conv_out, num_classes)
        
        self._initialize_weights()
    
    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.first_conv(x)
        x = self.blocks(x)
        x = self.last_conv(x)
        x = self.avgpool(x)
        x = x.view(x.size(0), -1)
        x = self.dropout(x)
        x = self.classifier(x)
        return x
    
    def _initialize_weights(self):
        for m in self.modules():
            if isinstance(m, nn.Conv2d):
                nn.init.kaiming_normal_(m.weight, mode='fan_out')
                if m.bias is not None:
                    nn.init.zeros_(m.bias)
            elif isinstance(m, nn.BatchNorm2d):

                nn.init.zeros_(m.bias)

def test_models():
    """
    Test all models with sample input to verify functionality
    """
    print("=" * 80)
    print("Testing Lightweight Architecture Patterns")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Sample input
    batch_size = 2
    x = torch.randn(batch_size, 3, 224, 224)
    
    models = {
        'MobileNet v1': MobileNetV1(num_classes=1000, width_multiplier=1.0),
        'MobileNet v2': MobileNetV2(num_classes=1000, width_mult=1.0),
        'MobileNet v3 Large': MobileNetV3(mode='large', num_classes=1000),
        'MobileNet v3 Small': MobileNetV3(mode='small', num_classes=1000),
        'ShuffleNet v1': ShuffleNetV1(num_classes=1000, groups=3),
        'ShuffleNet v2 1.0x': ShuffleNetV2(num_classes=1000, model_size='1.0x'),
        'GhostNet': GhostNet(num_classes=1000, width_mult=1.0),
        'ESPNet': ESPNet(num_classes=1000, scale=1.0),
        'EfficientNet-Lite': EfficientNetLite(num_classes=1000),
        'MicroNet': MicroNet(num_classes=1000, width_mult=1.0),
        'MCUNet-in3': MCUNet(num_classes=1000, net_config='mcunet-in3'),
    }
    
    for name, model in models.items():
        model.eval()
        
        # Count parameters
        total_params = sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())
        trainable_params = sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters() 
                              if p.requires_grad)
        
        # Test forward pass
        with torch.no_grad():
            output = model(x)
        
        print(f"\n{name}:")
        print(f"  Total Parameters: {total_params:,}")
        print(f"  Trainable Parameters: {trainable_params:,}")
        print(f"  Output shape: {output.shape}")
        print(f"  Memory (approx): {total_params * 4 / 1024 / 1024:.2f} MB")


def compare_efficiency():
    """
    Compare computational efficiency of different models
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("Model Efficiency Comparison")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    from thop import profile, clever_format
    
    x = torch.randn(1, 3, 224, 224)
    
    models_to_compare = {
        'MobileNet v1 (1.0x)': MobileNetV1(width_multiplier=1.0),
        'MobileNet v1 (0.5x)': MobileNetV1(width_multiplier=0.5),
        'MobileNet v2': MobileNetV2(width_mult=1.0),
        'MobileNet v3 Large': MobileNetV3(mode='large'),
        'MobileNet v3 Small': MobileNetV3(mode='small'),
        'ShuffleNet v2 1.0x': ShuffleNetV2(model_size='1.0x'),
        'ShuffleNet v2 0.5x': ShuffleNetV2(model_size='0.5x'),
        'GhostNet': GhostNet(width_mult=1.0),
        'EfficientNet-Lite': EfficientNetLite(),
        'MicroNet': MicroNet(width_mult=1.0),
        'MCUNet': MCUNet(net_config='mcunet-in3'),
    }
    
    print(f"\n{'Model':<25} {'Params (M)':<15} {'FLOPs (M)':<15} {'Size (MB)':<15}")
    print("-" * 70)
    
    for name, model in models_to_compare.items():
        model.eval()
        
        # Count parameters
        params = sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters()) / 1e6
        
        # Calculate FLOPs
        try:
            flops, _ = profile(model, inputs=(x,), verbose=False)
            flops = flops / 1e6
        except:
            flops = 0  # If thop is not installed
        
        # Model size in MB
        size_mb = params * 4  # Assuming float32
        
        print(f"{name:<25} {params:<15.2f} {flops:<15.2f} {size_mb:<15.2f}")


def demonstrate_inference():
    """
    Demonstrate inference with different models
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("Inference Speed Comparison")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    import time
    
    device = torch.device('cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu')
    print(f"\nUsing device: {device}")
    
    x = torch.randn(1, 3, 224, 224).to(device)
    num_iterations = 100
    
    models_to_test = {
        'MobileNet v2': MobileNetV2(),
        'MobileNet v3 Small': MobileNetV3(mode='small'),
        'ShuffleNet v2 0.5x': ShuffleNetV2(model_size='0.5x'),
        'GhostNet': GhostNet(),
        'MicroNet': MicroNet(),
    }
    
    print(f"\n{'Model':<25} {'Avg Time (ms)':<20} {'FPS':<15}")
    print("-" * 60)
    
    for name, model in models_to_test.items():
        model = model.to(device)
        model.eval()
        
        # Warmup
        with torch.no_grad():
            for _ in range(10):
                _ = model(x)
        
        # Measure inference time
        if device.type == 'cuda':
            torch.cuda.synchronize()
        
        start_time = time.time()
        with torch.no_grad():
            for _ in range(num_iterations):
                _ = model(x)
        
        if device.type == 'cuda':
            torch.cuda.synchronize()
        
        elapsed_time = time.time() - start_time
        avg_time_ms = (elapsed_time / num_iterations) * 1000
        fps = 1000 / avg_time_ms
        
        print(f"{name:<25} {avg_time_ms:<20.2f} {fps:<15.2f}")

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F
from typing import Optional, Callable

# ============================================================================
# 1. INVERTED BOTTLENECK (MobileNetV2 style)
# ============================================================================
class InvertedBottleneck(nn.Module):
    """
    Inverted Bottleneck block - expands channels, applies depthwise conv, then projects back.
    
    Architecture Flow:
    Input (C_in) -> Expand (C_in * expansion) -> DepthwiseConv -> Project (C_out)
    
    Key Features:
    - Expands narrow input to wide intermediate representation
    - Uses depthwise separable convolutions for efficiency
    - Optional residual connection when stride=1 and in_channels=out_channels
    
    Args:
        in_channels: Number of input channels
        out_channels: Number of output channels
        expansion: Expansion ratio for intermediate channels
        stride: Stride for depthwise convolution
        activation: Activation function (default: ReLU6)
    """
    def __init__(
        self, 
        in_channels: int,
        out_channels: int,
        expansion: int = 6,
        stride: int = 1,
        activation: nn.Module = nn.ReLU6(inplace=True)
    ):
        super(InvertedBottleneck, self).__init__()
        
        self.stride = stride
        self.use_residual = (stride == 1 and in_channels == out_channels)
        hidden_dim = in_channels * expansion
        
        layers = []
        
        # Expansion phase (only if expansion > 1)
        if expansion != 1:
            layers.extend([
                nn.Conv2d(in_channels, hidden_dim, kernel_size=1, bias=False),
                nn.BatchNorm2d(hidden_dim),
                activation
            ])
        
        # Depthwise convolution phase
        layers.extend([
            nn.Conv2d(
                hidden_dim, hidden_dim, 
                kernel_size=3, stride=stride, 
                padding=1, groups=hidden_dim, bias=False
            ),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(hidden_dim),
            activation,
            # Projection phase (linear bottleneck - no activation)
            nn.Conv2d(hidden_dim, out_channels, kernel_size=1, bias=False),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(out_channels)
        ])
        
        self.conv = nn.Sequential(*layers)
    
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        if self.use_residual:
            return x + self.conv(x)
        else:
            return self.conv(x)


# ============================================================================
# 2. LINEAR BOTTLENECK
# ============================================================================
class LinearBottleneck(nn.Module):
    """
    Linear Bottleneck - reduces dimensionality without non-linear activation.
    
    Architecture Flow:
    Input (C_in) -> Conv1x1 (C_bottleneck) -> [Optional: Conv3x3] -> Conv1x1 (C_out)
    
    Key Features:
    - Preserves information by avoiding non-linearity at bottleneck
    - Reduces computational complexity
    - Commonly used in MobileNets and EfficientNets
    
    Args:
        in_channels: Number of input channels
        out_channels: Number of output channels
        bottleneck_channels: Number of bottleneck channels
        use_conv3x3: Whether to include 3x3 conv in bottleneck
        stride: Stride for middle convolution
    """
    def __init__(
        self,
        in_channels: int,
        out_channels: int,
        bottleneck_channels: int,
        use_conv3x3: bool = True,
        stride: int = 1
    ):
        super(LinearBottleneck, self).__init__()
        
        self.use_residual = (stride == 1 and in_channels == out_channels)
        
        # Bottleneck reduction
        self.reduce = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(in_channels, bottleneck_channels, kernel_size=1, bias=False),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(bottleneck_channels),
            nn.ReLU6(inplace=True)
        )
        
        # Optional middle convolution
        if use_conv3x3:
            self.middle = nn.Sequential(
                nn.Conv2d(
                    bottleneck_channels, bottleneck_channels,
                    kernel_size=3, stride=stride, padding=1, bias=False
                ),
                nn.BatchNorm2d(bottleneck_channels),
                nn.ReLU6(inplace=True)
            )
        else:
            self.middle = nn.Identity()
        
        # Linear expansion (no activation - this is the key feature)
        self.expand = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(bottleneck_channels, out_channels, kernel_size=1, bias=False),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(out_channels)
            # Note: NO activation here - linear bottleneck
        )
    
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        identity = x
        out = self.reduce(x)
        out = self.middle(out)
        out = self.expand(out)
        
        if self.use_residual:
            out = out + identity
        
        return out


# ============================================================================
# 3. EXPANSION LAYER
# ============================================================================
class ExpansionLayer(nn.Module):
    """
    Expansion Layer - increases channel dimensionality for richer representations.
    
    Architecture Flow:
    Input (C_in) -> Conv (C_in * expansion_ratio) -> Activation
    
    Key Features:
    - Increases feature map capacity
    - Can use 1x1 or 3x3 convolutions
    - Often used before computationally intensive operations
    
    Args:
        in_channels: Number of input channels
        expansion_ratio: Ratio to expand channels
        kernel_size: Size of convolution kernel (1 or 3)
        activation: Activation function
        use_depthwise: Whether to use depthwise separable convolution
    """
    def __init__(
        self,
        in_channels: int,
        expansion_ratio: int = 6,
        kernel_size: int = 1,
        activation: Optional[nn.Module] = None,
        use_depthwise: bool = False
    ):
        super(ExpansionLayer, self).__init__()
        
        if activation is None:
            activation = nn.ReLU6(inplace=True)
        
        out_channels = in_channels * expansion_ratio
        padding = (kernel_size - 1) // 2
        
        if use_depthwise and kernel_size > 1:
            # Depthwise separable expansion
            self.expand = nn.Sequential(
                # Pointwise expansion
                nn.Conv2d(in_channels, out_channels, kernel_size=1, bias=False),
                nn.BatchNorm2d(out_channels),
                activation,
                # Depthwise convolution
                nn.Conv2d(
                    out_channels, out_channels,
                    kernel_size=kernel_size, padding=padding,
                    groups=out_channels, bias=False
                ),
                nn.BatchNorm2d(out_channels),
                activation
            )
        else:
            # Standard expansion
            self.expand = nn.Sequential(
                nn.Conv2d(
                    in_channels, out_channels,
                    kernel_size=kernel_size, padding=padding, bias=False
                ),
                nn.BatchNorm2d(out_channels),
                activation
            )
    
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        return self.expand(x)


# ============================================================================
# 4. PROJECTION LAYER
# ============================================================================
class ProjectionLayer(nn.Module):
    """
    Projection Layer - reduces dimensionality and projects features to new space.
    
    Architecture Flow:
    Input (C_in) -> Conv1x1 (C_out) -> [Optional: Activation]
    
    Key Features:
    - Dimensionality reduction
    - Cross-channel information mixing
    - Can be linear (no activation) or non-linear
    
    Args:
        in_channels: Number of input channels
        out_channels: Number of output channels
        use_activation: Whether to apply activation (False for linear projection)
        activation: Activation function to use
        use_dropout: Whether to add dropout
        dropout_rate: Dropout probability
    """
    def __init__(
        self,
        in_channels: int,
        out_channels: int,
        use_activation: bool = False,
        activation: Optional[nn.Module] = None,
        use_dropout: bool = False,
        dropout_rate: float = 0.1
    ):
        super(ProjectionLayer, self).__init__()
        
        layers = [
            nn.Conv2d(in_channels, out_channels, kernel_size=1, bias=False),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(out_channels)
        ]
        
        if use_activation:
            if activation is None:
                activation = nn.ReLU6(inplace=True)
            layers.append(activation)
        
        if use_dropout:
            layers.append(nn.Dropout2d(p=dropout_rate))
        
        self.project = nn.Sequential(*layers)
    
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        return self.project(x)


# ============================================================================
# 5. TRANSITION LAYER
# ============================================================================
class TransitionLayer(nn.Module):
    """
    Transition Layer - changes spatial/channel dimensions between network stages.
    
    Architecture Flow:
    Input -> [Compression] -> [Pooling/Strided Conv] -> Output
    
    Key Features:
    - Reduces feature map size and/or channels
    - Used between dense blocks or network stages
    - Can use pooling or strided convolutions
    
    Args:
        in_channels: Number of input channels
        out_channels: Number of output channels (None for compression ratio)
        compression: Compression ratio for channels (if out_channels is None)
        use_pooling: Use average pooling (True) or strided conv (False)
        pool_size: Size of pooling kernel
        activation: Activation function
    """
    def __init__(
        self,
        in_channels: int,
        out_channels: Optional[int] = None,
        compression: float = 0.5,
        use_pooling: bool = True,
        pool_size: int = 2,
        activation: Optional[nn.Module] = None
    ):
        super(TransitionLayer, self).__init__()
        
        if out_channels is None:
            out_channels = int(in_channels * compression)
        
        if activation is None:
            activation = nn.ReLU(inplace=True)
        
        # Compression phase
        self.compress = nn.Sequential(
            nn.BatchNorm2d(in_channels),
            activation,
            nn.Conv2d(in_channels, out_channels, kernel_size=1, bias=False)
        )
        
        # Downsampling phase
        if use_pooling:
            self.downsample = nn.AvgPool2d(kernel_size=pool_size, stride=pool_size)
        else:
            self.downsample = nn.Sequential(
                nn.BatchNorm2d(out_channels),
                activation,
                nn.Conv2d(
                    out_channels, out_channels,
                    kernel_size=3, stride=2, padding=1, bias=False
                )
            )
    
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        x = self.compress(x)
        x = self.downsample(x)
        return x


# ============================================================================
# 6. FUSION LAYER
# ============================================================================
class FusionLayer(nn.Module):
    """
    Fusion Layer - combines multiple feature maps from different sources/scales.
    
    Supported Fusion Methods:
    - 'concat': Concatenation along channel dimension
    - 'add': Element-wise addition (requires same channels)
    - 'attention': Attention-weighted fusion
    - 'weighted': Learnable weighted sum
    
    Key Features:
    - Multi-scale feature integration
    - Cross-path information flow
    - Flexible fusion strategies
    
    Args:
        fusion_type: Type of fusion ('concat', 'add', 'attention', 'weighted')
        num_inputs: Number of input feature maps to fuse
        in_channels_list: List of input channels for each input
        out_channels: Output channels (for concat fusion with projection)
        use_projection: Whether to project fused features
    """
    def __init__(
        self,
        fusion_type: str = 'concat',
        num_inputs: int = 2,
        in_channels_list: Optional[list] = None,
        out_channels: Optional[int] = None,
        use_projection: bool = True
    ):
        super(FusionLayer, self).__init__()
        
        self.fusion_type = fusion_type.lower()
        self.num_inputs = num_inputs
        
        if in_channels_list is None:
            in_channels_list = [64] * num_inputs
        
        self.in_channels_list = in_channels_list
        
        # Concatenation fusion
        if self.fusion_type == 'concat':
            total_channels = sum(in_channels_list)
            if out_channels is None:
                out_channels = total_channels
            
            if use_projection:
                self.projection = nn.Sequential(
                    nn.Conv2d(total_channels, out_channels, kernel_size=1, bias=False),
                    nn.BatchNorm2d(out_channels),
                    nn.ReLU(inplace=True)
                )
            else:
                self.projection = nn.Identity()
        
        # Addition fusion (requires channel alignment)
        elif self.fusion_type == 'add':
            # Ensure all inputs have same channels or add projection layers
            if len(set(in_channels_list)) > 1:
                target_channels = max(in_channels_list)
                self.align_layers = nn.ModuleList([
                    nn.Conv2d(in_ch, target_channels, kernel_size=1, bias=False)
                    if in_ch != target_channels else nn.Identity()
                    for in_ch in in_channels_list
                ])
            else:
                self.align_layers = nn.ModuleList([nn.Identity()] * num_inputs)
        
        # Attention-based fusion
        elif self.fusion_type == 'attention':
            # Channel attention for each input
            self.attention_weights = nn.ModuleList([
                nn.Sequential(
                    nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1),
                    nn.Conv2d(in_ch, in_ch // 4, kernel_size=1),
                    nn.ReLU(inplace=True),
                    nn.Conv2d(in_ch // 4, in_ch, kernel_size=1),
                    nn.Sigmoid()
                )
                for in_ch in in_channels_list
            ])
            
            # Ensure same channels for fusion
            if len(set(in_channels_list)) > 1:
                target_channels = max(in_channels_list)
                self.align_layers = nn.ModuleList([
                    nn.Conv2d(in_ch, target_channels, kernel_size=1, bias=False)
                    if in_ch != target_channels else nn.Identity()
```python
                    if in_ch != target_channels else nn.Identity()
                    for in_ch in in_channels_list
                ])
            else:
                self.align_layers = nn.ModuleList([nn.Identity()] * num_inputs)
        
        # Learnable weighted fusion
        elif self.fusion_type == 'weighted':
            # Learnable weights for each input
            self.fusion_weights = nn.Parameter(torch.ones(num_inputs))
            
            # Ensure same channels for fusion
            if len(set(in_channels_list)) > 1:
                target_channels = max(in_channels_list)
                self.align_layers = nn.ModuleList([
                    nn.Conv2d(in_ch, target_channels, kernel_size=1, bias=False)
                    if in_ch != target_channels else nn.Identity()
                    for in_ch in in_channels_list
                ])
            else:
                self.align_layers = nn.ModuleList([nn.Identity()] * num_inputs)
        
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported fusion type: {fusion_type}")
    
    def forward(self, inputs: list) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Args:
            inputs: List of input tensors to fuse
        
        Returns:
            Fused output tensor
        """
        assert len(inputs) == self.num_inputs, \
            f"Expected {self.num_inputs} inputs, got {len(inputs)}"
        
        # Ensure all inputs have same spatial dimensions
        target_size = inputs[0].shape[2:]
        aligned_inputs = []
        for x in inputs:
            if x.shape[2:] != target_size:
                x = F.interpolate(x, size=target_size, mode='bilinear', align_corners=False)
            aligned_inputs.append(x)
        
        # Apply fusion based on type
        if self.fusion_type == 'concat':
            # Concatenate along channel dimension
            fused = torch.cat(aligned_inputs, dim=1)
            output = self.projection(fused)
        
        elif self.fusion_type == 'add':
            # Element-wise addition with channel alignment
            aligned = [self.align_layers[i](x) for i, x in enumerate(aligned_inputs)]
            output = torch.stack(aligned, dim=0).sum(dim=0)
        
        elif self.fusion_type == 'attention':
            # Attention-weighted fusion
            aligned = [self.align_layers[i](x) for i, x in enumerate(aligned_inputs)]
            weighted = []
            for i, x in enumerate(aligned):
                attention = self.attention_weights[i](x)
                weighted.append(x * attention)
            output = torch.stack(weighted, dim=0).sum(dim=0)
        
        elif self.fusion_type == 'weighted':
            # Learnable weighted fusion with softmax normalization
            aligned = [self.align_layers[i](x) for i, x in enumerate(aligned_inputs)]
            weights = F.softmax(self.fusion_weights, dim=0)
            weighted = [w * x for w, x in zip(weights, aligned)]
            output = torch.stack(weighted, dim=0).sum(dim=0)
        
        return output

class CompleteExampleNetwork(nn.Module):

    Example network demonstrating how to combine all components together.
    
    Architecture:
    1. Initial Conv
    2. Inverted Bottleneck blocks
    3. Transition layer
    4. Linear Bottleneck
    5. Multi-path with Fusion
    6. Final Projection
    """
    def __init__(self, num_classes: int = 1000):
        super(CompleteExampleNetwork, self).__init__()
        
        # Initial convolution
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(3, 32, kernel_size=3, stride=2, padding=1, bias=False),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(32),
            nn.ReLU6(inplace=True)
        )
        
        # Stage 1: Inverted Bottlenecks
        self.stage1 = nn.Sequential(
            InvertedBottleneck(32, 64, expansion=6, stride=2),
            InvertedBottleneck(64, 64, expansion=6, stride=1),
        )
        
        # Transition to next stage
        self.transition1 = TransitionLayer(
            in_channels=64,
            out_channels=128,
            use_pooling=False
        )
        
        # Stage 2: Linear Bottlenecks
        self.stage2 = nn.Sequential(
            LinearBottleneck(128, 128, bottleneck_channels=32),
            LinearBottleneck(128, 128, bottleneck_channels=32),
        )
        
        # Multi-path processing
        self.path1 = ExpansionLayer(128, expansion_ratio=2, kernel_size=3)
        self.path2 = nn.Sequential(
            ExpansionLayer(128, expansion_ratio=2, kernel_size=1),
            nn.Conv2d(256, 256, kernel_size=3, padding=1, groups=256),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(256),
            nn.ReLU6(inplace=True)
        )
        
        # Fusion of multiple paths
        self.fusion = FusionLayer(
            fusion_type='attention',
            num_inputs=2,
            in_channels_list=[256, 256]
        )
        
        # Final projection and classification
        self.final_projection = ProjectionLayer(
            in_channels=256,
            out_channels=512,
            use_activation=True
        )
        
        self.global_pool = nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1)
        self.classifier = nn.Linear(512, num_classes)
    
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        # Initial processing
        x = self.stem(x)  # [B, 3, H, W] -> [B, 32, H/2, W/2]
        
        # Stage 1
        x = self.stage1(x)  # [B, 32, H/2, W/2]
```python
        x = self.stage1(x)  # [B, 32, H/2, W/2] -> [B, 64, H/4, W/4]
        
        # Transition
        x = self.transition1(x)  # [B, 64, H/4, W/4] -> [B, 128, H/8, W/8]
        
        # Stage 2
        x = self.stage2(x)  # [B, 128, H/8, W/8]
        
        # Multi-path processing
        path1_out = self.path1(x)  # [B, 128, H/8, W/8] -> [B, 256, H/8, W/8]
        path2_out = self.path2(x)  # [B, 128, H/8, W/8] -> [B, 256, H/8, W/8]
        
        # Fuse paths
        x = self.fusion([path1_out, path2_out])  # [B, 256, H/8, W/8]
        
        # Final processing
        x = self.final_projection(x)  # [B, 256, H/8, W/8] -> [B, 512, H/8, W/8]
        x = self.global_pool(x)  # [B, 512, H/8, W/8] -> [B, 512, 1, 1]
        x = torch.flatten(x, 1)  # [B, 512, 1, 1] -> [B, 512]
        x = self.classifier(x)  # [B, 512] -> [B, num_classes]
        
        return x

class AdvancedUsageExamples:
    """
    Advanced usage patterns and combinations of the components.
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_mobile_block(in_channels: int, out_channels: int, stride: int = 1):
        """
        Creates a MobileNetV2-style block using Inverted Bottleneck.
        """
        return nn.Sequential(
            InvertedBottleneck(in_channels, out_channels, expansion=6, stride=stride),
            InvertedBottleneck(out_channels, out_channels, expansion=6, stride=1),
            InvertedBottleneck(out_channels, out_channels, expansion=6, stride=1)
        )
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_efficient_block(in_channels: int, out_channels: int):
        """
        Creates an EfficientNet-style block with squeeze-excitation.
        """
        class SEBlock(nn.Module):
            def __init__(self, channels, reduction=4):
                super().__init__()
                self.se = nn.Sequential(
                    nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1),
                    nn.Conv2d(channels, channels // reduction, 1),
                    nn.ReLU(inplace=True),
                    nn.Conv2d(channels // reduction, channels, 1),
                    nn.Sigmoid()
                )
            
            def forward(self, x):
                return x * self.se(x)
        
        return nn.Sequential(
            InvertedBottleneck(in_channels, out_channels, expansion=6, stride=2),
            SEBlock(out_channels),
            InvertedBottleneck(out_channels, out_channels, expansion=6, stride=1)
        )
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_densenet_transition(in_channels: int, compression: float = 0.5):
        """
        Creates a DenseNet-style transition layer.
        """
        return TransitionLayer(
            in_channels=in_channels,
            compression=compression,
            use_pooling=True,
            pool_size=2
        )
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_fpn_fusion(channel_list: list):
        """
        Creates a Feature Pyramid Network-style fusion.
        """
        return FusionLayer(
            fusion_type='concat',
            num_inputs=len(channel_list),
            in_channels_list=channel_list,
            out_channels=max(channel_list),
            use_projection=True
        )
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_multi_scale_block(in_channels: int):
        """
        Creates a multi-scale processing block with parallel paths.
        """
        class MultiScaleBlock(nn.Module):
            def __init__(self, channels):
                super().__init__()
                
                # Path 1: 1x1 convolution
                self.path1 = ProjectionLayer(channels, channels, use_activation=True)
                
                # Path 2: 3x3 convolution
                self.path2 = nn.Sequential(
                    nn.Conv2d(channels, channels, 3, padding=1, bias=False),
                    nn.BatchNorm2d(channels),
                    nn.ReLU(inplace=True)
                )
                
                # Path 3: 5x5 convolution (as 2x 3x3)
                self.path3 = nn.Sequential(
                    nn.Conv2d(channels, channels, 3, padding=1, bias=False),
                    nn.BatchNorm2d(channels),
                    nn.ReLU(inplace=True),
                    nn.Conv2d(channels, channels, 3, padding=1, bias=False),
                    nn.BatchNorm2d(channels),
                    nn.ReLU(inplace=True)
                )
                
                # Fusion
                self.fusion = FusionLayer(
                    fusion_type='concat',
                    num_inputs=3,
                    in_channels_list=[channels, channels, channels],
                    out_channels=channels,
                    use_projection=True
                )
            
            def forward(self, x):
                p1 = self.path1(x)
                p2 = self.path2(x)
                p3 = self.path3(x)
                return self.fusion([p1, p2, p3])
        
        return MultiScaleBlock(in_channels)

def benchmark_components():
    """
    Benchmarks the computational efficiency of each component.
    """
    import time
    
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("PERFORMANCE BENCHMARKING")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    device = torch.device('cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu')
    print(f"\nDevice: {device}")
    
    batch_size = 32
    height, width = 56, 56
    num_iterations = 100
    
    components = {
        'Inverted Bottleneck': InvertedBottleneck(64, 128, expansion=6, stride=1),
        'Linear Bottleneck': LinearBottleneck(128, 128, bottleneck_channels=32),
        'Expansion Layer': ExpansionLayer(64, expansion_ratio=4),
        'Projection Layer': ProjectionLayer(256, 128, use_activation=True),
        'Transition Layer': TransitionLayer(256, compression=0.5),
        'Fusion (Concat)': FusionLayer('concat', 2, [64, 64], 128),
        'Fusion (Attention)': FusionLayer('attention', 2, [64, 64])
    }
    
    print(f"\nBenchmarking with batch_size={batch_size}, size={height}x{width}")
    print(f"Iterations: {num_iterations}")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    for name, component in components.items():
        component = component.to(device)
        component.eval()
        
        # Prepare input
        if 'Fusion' in name:
            inputs = [
                torch.randn(batch_size, 64, height, width, device=device),
                torch.randn(batch_size, 64, height, width, device=device)
            ]
        elif 'Inverted' in name or 'Expansion' in name:
            inputs = torch.randn(batch_size, 64, height, width, device=device)
        elif 'Projection' in name or 'Transition' in name:
            inputs = torch.randn(batch_size, 256, height, width, device=device)
        else:
            inputs = torch.randn(batch_size, 128, height, width, device=device)
        
        # Warmup
        with torch.no_grad():
            for _ in range(10):
                if isinstance(inputs, list):
                    _ = component(inputs)
                else:
                    _ = component(inputs)
        
        # Benchmark
        if device.type == 'cuda':
            torch.cuda.synchronize()
        
        start_time = time.time()
        with torch.no_grad():
            for _ in range(num_iterations):
                if isinstance(inputs, list):
                    _ = component(inputs)
                else:
                    _ = component(inputs)
        
        if device.type == 'cuda':
            torch.cuda.synchronize()
        
        end_time = time.time()
        avg_time = (end_time - start_time) / num_iterations * 1000  # ms
        
        params = sum(p.numel() for p in component.parameters())
        
        print(f"{name:25} | Time: {avg_time:6.2f}ms | Params: {params:8,}")

# ADDITIONAL UTILITY FUNCTIONS
# ============================================================================
class ComponentFactory:
    """
    Factory class for creating common component combinations.
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_mbconv_block(
        in_channels: int,
        out_channels: int,
        expansion: int = 6,
        stride: int = 1,
        use_se: bool = True,
        se_ratio: float = 0.25
    ):
        """
        Creates a MBConv block (Mobile Inverted Bottleneck Convolution).
        Used in EfficientNet and MobileNetV3.
        
        Args:
            in_channels: Input channels
            out_channels: Output channels
            expansion: Expansion ratio
            stride: Stride for depthwise conv
            use_se: Whether to use Squeeze-and-Excitation
            se_ratio: Reduction ratio for SE block
        """
        class MBConvBlock(nn.Module):
            def __init__(self):
                super().__init__()
                self.use_residual = (stride == 1 and in_channels == out_channels)
                hidden_dim = in_channels * expansion
                
                layers = []
                
                # Expansion
                if expansion != 1:
                    layers.extend([
                        nn.Conv2d(in_channels, hidden_dim, 1, bias=False),
                        nn.BatchNorm2d(hidden_dim),
                        nn.ReLU6(inplace=True)
                    ])
                
                # Depthwise
                layers.extend([
                    nn.Conv2d(hidden_dim, hidden_dim, 3, stride=stride, 
                             padding=1, groups=hidden_dim, bias=False),
                    nn.BatchNorm2d(hidden_dim),
                    nn.ReLU6(inplace=True)
                ])
                
                self.conv = nn.Sequential(*layers)
                
                # Squeeze-and-Excitation
                if use_se:
                    se_channels = max(1, int(in_channels * se_ratio))
                    self.se = nn.Sequential(
                        nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1),
                        nn.Conv2d(hidden_dim, se_channels, 1),
                        nn.ReLU(inplace=True),
                        nn.Conv2d(se_channels, hidden_dim, 1),
                        nn.Sigmoid()
                    )
                else:
                    self.se = None
                
                # Projection
                self.project = nn.Sequential(
                    nn.Conv2d(hidden_dim, out_channels, 1, bias=False),
                    nn.BatchNorm2d(out_channels)
                )
            
            def forward(self, x):
                identity = x
                out = self.conv(x)
                
                if self.se is not None:
                    out = out * self.se(out)
                
                out = self.project(out)
                
                if self.use_residual:
                    out = out + identity
                
                return out
        
        return MBConvBlock()
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_fused_mbconv(
        in_channels: int,
        out_channels: int,
        expansion: int = 4,
        stride: int = 1
    ):
        """
        Creates a Fused-MBConv block (used in EfficientNetV2).
        Replaces depthwise conv with regular conv for better training speed.
        """
        class FusedMBConv(nn.Module):
            def __init__(self):
                super().__init__()
                self.use_residual = (stride == 1 and in_channels == out_channels)
                hidden_dim = in_channels * expansion
                
                # Fused expansion + spatial conv
                self.expand = nn.Sequential(
                    nn.Conv2d(in_channels, hidden_dim, 3, stride=stride, 
                             padding=1, bias=False),
                    nn.BatchNorm2d(hidden_dim),
                    nn.ReLU(inplace=True)
                )
                
                # Projection
                self.project = nn.Sequential(
                    nn.Conv2d(hidden_dim, out_channels, 1, bias=False),
                    nn.BatchNorm2d(out_channels)
                )
            
            def forward(self, x):
                identity = x
                out = self.expand(x)
                out = self.project(out)
                
                if self.use_residual:
                    out = out + identity
                
                return out
        
        return FusedMBConv()
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_bifpn_fusion(num_inputs: int, channels: int):
        """
        Creates a BiFPN (Bidirectional Feature Pyramid Network) fusion node.
        Uses weighted fusion with fast normalized fusion.
        """
        class BiFPNFusion(nn.Module):
            def __init__(self):
                super().__init__()
                self.weights = nn.Parameter(torch.ones(num_inputs))
                self.epsilon = 1e-4
                
                # Depthwise separable conv after fusion
                self.conv = nn.Sequential(
                    nn.Conv2d(channels, channels, 3, padding=1, 
                             groups=channels, bias=False),
                    nn.BatchNorm2d(channels),
                    nn.Conv2d(channels, channels, 1, bias=False),
                    nn.BatchNorm2d(channels),
                    nn.ReLU(inplace=True)
                )
            
            def forward(self, inputs):
                # Fast normalized fusion
                weights = F.relu(self.weights)
                weights = weights / (weights.sum() + self.epsilon)
                
                # Resize all inputs to same size
                target_size = inputs[0].shape[2:]
                resized = []
                for x in inputs:
                    if x.shape[2:] != target_size:
                        x = F.interpolate(x, size=target_size, 
                                        mode='nearest')
                    resized.append(x)
                
                # Weighted sum
                fused = sum(w * x for w, x in zip(weights, resized))
                
                # Apply convolution
                return self.conv(fused)
        
        return BiFPNFusion()
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_residual_bottleneck(
        in_channels: int,
        out_channels: int,
        bottleneck_ratio: float = 0.25,
        stride: int = 1
    ):
        """
        Creates a ResNet-style bottleneck block.
        """
        bottleneck_channels = int(out_channels * bottleneck_ratio)
        
        class ResidualBottleneck(nn.Module):
            def __init__(self):
                super().__init__()
                
                self.conv1 = nn.Sequential(
                    nn.Conv2d(in_channels, bottleneck_channels, 1, bias=False),
                    nn.BatchNorm2d(bottleneck_channels),
                    nn.ReLU(inplace=True)
                )
                
                self.conv2 = nn.Sequential(
                    nn.Conv2d(bottleneck_channels, bottleneck_channels, 3,
                             stride=stride, padding=1, bias=False),
                    nn.BatchNorm2d(bottleneck_channels),
                    nn.ReLU(inplace=True)
                )
                
                self.conv3 = nn.Sequential(
                    nn.Conv2d(bottleneck_channels, out_channels, 1, bias=False),
                    nn.BatchNorm2d(out_channels)
                )
                
                # Shortcut
                if stride != 1 or in_channels != out_channels:
                    self.shortcut = nn.Sequential(
                        nn.Conv2d(in_channels, out_channels, 1, 
                                 stride=stride, bias=False),
                        nn.BatchNorm2d(out_channels)
                    )
                else:
                    self.shortcut = nn.Identity()
                
                self.relu = nn.ReLU(inplace=True)
            
            def forward(self, x):
                identity = self.shortcut(x)
                
                out = self.conv1(x)
                out = self.conv2(out)
                out = self.conv3(out)
                
                out = out + identity
                out = self.relu(out)
                
                return out
        
        return ResidualBottleneck()
